critique: The piece is sequentially correct but thin: each beat is one property on one layer. The mark sits inert once drawn, the 1s Sine In Out ring draw feels sluggish against the snappy Expo slash, and the hand-keyed wordmark settle (300→271→280 on Sine In Out) reads mechanical rather than springy. The 36px low-contrast tagline is undersized against the 150px wordmark and leaves the lockup bottom-light.

Tighten the ring draw to ~0.6s with an Expo/Quart Out. Give the mark a small reaction as the wordmark exits from behind it, such as a slight scale or rotation pulse or the slash nudging. Replace the keyed bounce with a single spring or overshoot ease. Enlarge the tagline to ~48–56px with a touch more contrast, and align its left edge exactly to the N (currently 12px off).

The comp runs 10s instead of the briefed 8s, so the attribution lands at 8.5–9.1s, outside the requested duration. Each phrase is a fade-up exit (2.3–2.6s, 4.5–4.8s, 6.3–6.6s) followed by the next word-reveal starting 0.1s later in the same spot, so the phrases swap in sequence instead of transitioning into each other. On top of that, the short 'Design is' line sits idle for about 1.4s and the 'how it works.' hero gets no bigger moment than its per-letter reveal.

Cut the timing to 8s and build real handoffs: have 'what it looks like.' push 'Design is not just' up and out, and have 'Design is' shrink or slide aside as 'how it / works.' scales in with an overshoot spring. Bring in the attribution at about 7.0s and hold to the end. Delete the dead 0s→exit 'Easy Ease' position and opacity keys that don't change anything.

The knob is a flat white ellipse with no drop shadow, and the track fill is RGB-interpolated so mid-transition (0.55s) it goes through a muddy grey-green; it reads less like an iOS control and more like a flat mockup, and there is no press or anticipation beat before the 0.4s toggle.

Give the knob a soft drop shadow and a brief press-squash (~0.3-0.4s) before travel, crossfade the track as a green layer fading in over the grey instead of lerping the hex, and replace the separate overshoot keys with a spring so the knob doesn't dead-stop at 432 before easing back.

Beat 2 is a 0.7s scale-down rather than a 'suck-in': the notes shrink to nothing in place while the shield pops up separately, and a 3s dead hold (4.7–7.8s) leaves a static shield on screen; beat 1's slow ±5° sine sway also reads as a gentle sway rather than anxious jitter.

Rebuild the middle 4s as one continuous handoff: bring the shield in first, then stagger the notes along curved paths into its mouth with stretch, rotation spin and a squash/bump on the shield as each one lands. Fill the hold with that action and replace the sine sway with fast, small, irregular wiggle on position and rotation, so beat 1 feels nervous and beat 3's glow follows directly from the vault closing.
All motion ends by 2.67s and the last 3.3s is a dead static hold; the value labels only fade and drift instead of counting up, so the data reveal feels flat and front-loaded.

Stretch the build across the 6s with a slower stagger and longer bar grows, have each value count up from 0 in sync with its bar, and give Q4 a stronger, later accent beat (overshoot settle plus a color or glow shift) that resolves into a short end hold.

Violet and mint orbs run on a 3s cycle with 140–200px amplitude, peaking near 400px/s, which reads as busy bobbing rather than calm drift; the dot 'grid' is only 4 vertical bands pulsing in a visible left-to-right sweep, not a gently breathing field.

Put every orb on the 6s period (or 12s via 0.5236 rad/s with 6s harmonics) at 60–100px amplitude, give them overlap/screen blending for richer colour mixing, and split the dots into ≥15 cells with a radial or noise-offset phase so the pulse feels organic.

The piece runs 6s instead of the briefed 10s, and the CTA beat is misbuilt: 'Available now' sits jammed against the top edge of the pill instead of centred, the pill and text land at 3.2s/3.45s off the 0.5s beat grid, and the whole thing then sits in a dead 1.4s hold, so the ending feels unfinished rather than confident.

Extend the comp to 10s on a strict 0.5s grid: give each feature word a 1-beat cut with a varied exit, hit the PULSE 2 slam with the flash, rings and a camera shake on a downbeat, then bring in a vertically centred CTA pill (text parented to the pill so they scale together) on the next downbeat. Use the extra time for a rhythmic pulse on the title/pill every beat and a decisive out at 10s.

The bounce falls flat after the drop. All six shapes do the same scripted 'jostle': a nudge and a spring back on the same 1.7s keyframe. The letters pop into view mid-air from y=690 with a 0.08s fade, make one parabolic hop, and settle on Quad Out with no rebound. It reads as a templated stagger, not elastic, trampoline-like physics, and the shapes sit dead from 2.1s to 3.6s.

Make the letters drop in from above and land with a decaying spring: 2-3 shrinking bounces, with squash on each contact and a stretch on each rise. Have each landing knock the nearest candy shape with its own offset spring so the jostle is a real reaction. Start the idle wiggle earlier and include a slight scale or y bob, not just a ±4-5° rotation.

The build sequence inverts the brief and stays generic: the panel fades and slides in first (0.2s) and the accent line only starts at 0.6s, so the line does not lead with the panel arriving behind it. The name and title are plain opacity-plus-offset fades with no mask. The near-invisible 60% #1c2733 panel on #2a3440, at 800px wide, leaves a large empty right half.

Rebuild the intro as a choreographed chain. Start with the accent line scaling from a left anchor (0.2–1.0s, long Quart/expo in-out). Slide the panel in from that line with a slight width or clip reveal. Reveal the name and title through track mattes or masks wiping up from the line, staggered about 0.15s. Trim the panel to hug the text with a little more contrast so it reads as premium glass. Reverse the same chain on the way out.

The 'hand-drawn boil' is fake: an unposterized wiggle(8, 0.8) on position just jitters each rigid path smoothly at 24fps, so the line shapes never wobble. The blobs' ±2% sine breathing is barely perceptible, and with everything settled by about 4.6s the piece reads as a clean vector logo build rather than hand-animated work.

Replace the position wiggles with real line boil: cycle 2-3 slightly redrawn path keyframes (or wiggle the path vertices) with posterizeTime(12) on strokes and blobs. Raise the blob breathing to about 5-8% with slight non-uniform x/y, and add a small rotate/scale settle on the name so the last 1.5s feels alive and friendly.

The piece is thin and front-loaded. The line's opacity snaps in over 0.5s, breaking the 'nothing fast' rule. After 5s the only event is a barely legible tagline fade, and the end hold is just 0.67s. The result reads as a competent but bare line-plus-letters fade, not a crafted luxury reveal.

Slow the line fade to at least 1.2s. Then add one restrained layer of depth: a soft champagne glint travelling along the line or across the letters around 5–6s. Raise the tagline's size and contrast slightly, and finish its fade by about 5.8s so the final lockup holds for at least 1.2s.

The three orange pulse-wave rings sit on top of the white mark ring at scale 100 and fade up to 90% opacity over the first 4–6s. This tints the ring salmon for most of the piece, then it snaps to white as each wave leaves, so the mark's own color is unstable. The waves also expand with Cubic In, so they accelerate away and are almost invisible (5.83s) instead of reading as a sharp hit on 5s and 6s.

Keep each wave at 0 opacity until its beat, then fire it on that beat: snap to about 80% at scale 100, expand to about 200 with a fast Expo/Cubic Out over roughly 0.5s, and fade with it. This keeps the ring a clean, consistent white and turns the post-drop beats into visible, punchy secondary hits.
